record.original_question: Let E be a normed linear space such that for every unit vector x ∈ E one has inf_{||y|| = 1} max{||x + y||, ||x - y||} = √2. Does it follow that E is linearly isometric to an inner-product space?

evidence.quote: Let E be a normed linear space such that for each x ∈ E, ||x|| = 1, we have inf max {||x+y||,||x-y||} = √2. Is then E linearly isometric with an inner product ||y|| = 1 space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $E$ be a real normed linear space with norm $\|\cdot\|$. Suppose that for every unit vector $x \in E$ (that is, every $x$ with $\|x\| = 1$) one has
$$\inf_{\substack{y \in E \\ \|y\| = 1}} \max\bigl\{\|x + y\|,\ \|x - y\|\bigr\} = \sqrt{2}.$$
Does it follow that $E$ is linearly isometric to an inner-product space?
artifact.category_tag: Geometry of Banach spaces / inner-product characterizations
artifact.status_search_result: A targeted web search did not return any source that resolves this specific characterization of inner-product spaces via the equality $\inf_{\|y\|=1}\max\{\|x+y\|,\|x-y\|\}=\sqrt{2}$ for all unit vectors $x$. The standard inner-product characterizations found (parallelogram law, Day–James, etc.) do not directly settle the question, and no definitive solution could be located.

status_evidence.title: Inner product space - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Lists standard characterizations of inner-product spaces among normed spaces (parallelogram law, etc.) but does not include this specific inf-max condition.
status_evidence.claim: Standard known characterizations do not directly resolve the stated condition.
